interactives.title: Add one tenant: what lands on the switch, and what you write
interactives.caption: Captured from a Hedgehog VLAB. The left pane is the configuration that appeared on the switch when one tenant was added, taken as a before-and-after difference of the switch's own running config. The right pane is what the operator wrote to cause it.

left.label: What the switch ends up configured with

captured_from.system: Hedgehog VLAB: 1 spine, 2 SONiC VS leaves, 2 servers

left.baseline: Per-device configuration, as it would be authored by hand on each switch
left.representative_basis: The generated per-device configuration, which is exactly what would otherwise be written by hand. Taken as the difference of `sonic-cfggen -d` and `vtysh show running-config` on each switch, before and after one VPC and one VPCAttachment were applied; SONiC 4.5.2-Enterprise_Base. Counted as one line per configuration object rather than one line per field: expanding the fields would have given 76 lines instead of 35 on this device, padded with defaults nobody types, so the smaller number is used. Routing configuration is verbatim from the switch and already omits defaults.

captured_from.system: The VPC and VPCAttachment applied to that VLAB

equivalence.outcome: One tenant network exists on the fabric and server-01 is attached to it. Both panes describe the same applied state of the same fabric at the same moment.
